transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Well, lately I’ve noticed I’m not really taking in what people are saying, even when I’m looking right at them. Like at the museum, someone will be talking to me about the next art walk, and I’ll realize I missed the middle of it. Then I have to ask them to say it again. It’s been happening enough that it’s bothering me.
Do you find yourself getting distracted easily in other situations, like while reading, working, or trying to focus on a task?

Yes, especially when I’m reading something like a gallery packet or notes. I’ll start out okay, but after a few minutes I realize my eyes are still going down the page and my mind’s somewhere else. Then I have to go back and read the same section again.
Does this kind of difficulty with focus or attention happen in other situations as well, like when you're driving, having a conversation, or watching something?

Mostly I notice it in conversations. Like at the museum, someone will be talking right to me about the next art walk, and I’m looking at them, but then I realize I missed part of what they said. Then I have to ask them to go over it again.
Do you ever find yourself losing focus or missing details when you're doing tasks that require attention to detail, like organizing exhibits or preparing paperwork?

Yeah, mostly with reading through notes or gallery packets. I can start out fine, but after a few minutes I’ll realize my eyes are still moving over the page and I’m not really taking it in. Then I have to go back and read the same part again.
Do you find that this difficulty with staying focused happens in other places or activities, like at home, while driving, or during meetings?

Yeah, it does happen outside of just one place. The clearest example is when I sit down with a gallery packet or a set of notes. I’ll start off okay, but after a few minutes I notice my eyes are still going over the words and my mind has wandered. Then I have to go back and read the same part again.
Does this difficulty with staying focused happen even when you’re not reading or in work-related settings, like when you’re at home trying to relax or engage in a hobby?

I guess the main time I really notice it is still with things like packets or notes. I’ll sit down and start reading fine, but then after a few minutes I realize my eyes are still moving over the page and my mind’s gone somewhere else. Then I have to go back and read the same part again.
Do you ever have trouble staying focused even when you're doing something you enjoy, like watching a movie, talking with a friend, or working on a hobby?

Yeah, I’m not sure I notice it as much with movies or talking. The main thing I keep coming back to is reading notes or gallery packets. I’ll start out okay, but after a few minutes I realize my eyes are still going across the page and I’m not really taking it in, so I have to go back over the same part.

Can you think of a time when you were doing something you really enjoy, like being with friends or working on a personal project, where you also found it hard to stay focused or had to repeat parts to yourself?

I’m having a little trouble thinking of an example with friends or a personal project. The one that really stands out is still when I’m going through a gallery packet or notes. I’ll start off okay, but then a few minutes later I realize my eyes are still going across the page and I’m not actually taking it in. Then I have to go back and read the same part again.

Do you ever find it hard to stay focused or find your mind wandering when you're doing something that requires a lot of thinking, like planning an event or solving a problem, even if it's not related to reading or work notes?

I’m not sure I can think of a separate example like planning something. The clearest one for me is still when I sit down with a gallery packet or notes. I start out okay, but after a few minutes I’ll realize my eyes are still going over the page and my mind has drifted off, so I have to go back and read the same part again.

Can you think of a time when you were doing something that wasn’t work-related, like watching TV, reading for pleasure, or talking with a friend, where you found it hard to stay focused or realized your mind had wandered?

Not so much with TV or talking with someone, at least not that I can clearly remember. The example I keep thinking of is when I’m sitting with a gallery packet or some notes. I’ll be reading along, and then I realize I’ve been looking at the words but not really taking them in, so I have to go back and read that same section again.
Can you remember a time when you were in a conversation with someone or engaged in a leisure activity where you realized your mind had wandered and you had to bring your attention back?

Yes, that does happen. At the museum, someone will be talking right to me about the next art walk, and I’m looking at them like I’m listening, but then I realize I missed the middle part of what they said. Then I have to ask them to repeat it or run it by me again.
Can you remember if this kind of mind-wandering or losing focus happens to you during other kinds of activities, like talking with someone, watching something, or doing something you enjoy?

Yeah, mostly when someone’s talking to me. Like at the museum, people will be telling me about the next art walk, and I’m looking right at them, but then I realize I missed part of what they said. Usually the middle of it. Then I have to ask them to say it again or run it by me one more time.

Can you remember if there are times outside of conversations or reading—like when you're making a decision, doing something routine, or taking care of something—where you’ve noticed your mind wandering or realized you weren’t paying full attention?

Mostly what I notice is still with written stuff. Like I’ll sit down with a gallery packet or some notes and I start out okay, but after a few minutes my eyes are still moving across the page and my mind’s somewhere else. Then I realize I didn’t really take in what I just read, so I have to go back over the same part again.

Can you remember if there are times when you're making a decision, doing something routine, or taking care of something, where you've noticed your mind wandering or realized you weren't paying full attention?

The main thing I notice is when I sit down with something like a gallery packet or notes. I’ll start out reading it fine, but after a few minutes my eyes are still going over the words and my mind has drifted off. Then I realize I didn’t take in that part, so I have to go back and read it again.

Can you remember if there are times when you're doing something routine, like getting dressed or making a decision, where you've noticed your mind wandering or realized you weren't fully paying attention?

Yeah, I guess not so much with getting dressed or decisions that I can think of. It’s more when I sit down with something to read, like a gallery packet or some notes. I’ll start out okay, but after a few minutes I’m still looking at the page and my mind has gone somewhere else. Then I realize I didn’t really take it in, and I have to go back over the same part again.

Can you remember if there are times when you're doing something routine, like getting dressed or making a decision, where you've noticed your mind wandering or realized you weren't fully paying attention?

Not really with getting dressed or making decisions, at least nothing that stands out. What I notice more is with reading things, like a gallery packet or notes. I’ll start off okay, but after a few minutes I’m still looking at the words and my mind has kind of wandered off. Then I realize I didn’t take it in and I have to read that same part again.

Can you remember if there are times when you're doing something automatic, like walking, driving, or eating, where you realize your mind has wandered and you weren't really paying attention to what you were doing?

With things like walking or eating, I can’t really think of a clear example. What I do notice is more when I’m reading something, like a gallery packet or notes. I’ll start off fine, then a few minutes later my eyes are still moving along the page but my mind’s somewhere else, and I have to go back and read that part again.

Can you remember a time when you were doing something completely unrelated to work or reading—like talking with a friend, watching a movie, or relaxing—where you realized your mind had wandered and you had to bring your attention back?

I can’t really think of a clear time with talking to a friend or watching a movie. The main thing I’ve noticed is more when I’m reading, like a gallery packet or some notes. I’ll be looking right at the page, but after a few minutes my mind has drifted, and then I have to go back and read the same part again.

Can you remember if there are times when you're doing something that requires thinking, but isn't related to work or reading, like playing a game, planning something fun, or following a recipe, where you realized your mind had wandered and you had to go back or refocus?

I’m not sure with games or recipes, nothing really comes to mind there. The clearest thing for me is still when I sit down with a gallery packet or some notes. I’ll start reading and think I’m following it, but after a few minutes I’m just moving my eyes over the words and my mind has drifted off. Then I have to go back and read that same part again.

Can you remember if there are times when you're having a conversation, watching something, or doing a leisure activity where you realize your mind has wandered and you have to bring your attention back?

I still don’t really have a good example with a conversation or watching something. The thing I can point to is when I’m reading a gallery packet or notes. I’ll start out okay, but after a few minutes I realize my eyes are still going over the words and I’m not really taking it in, so I have to go back and read that part again.

target_item.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: I can sit down with a gallery packet or a set of notes and start out fine, but after a few minutes my eyes keep moving over the page while my mind has wandered off and I have to read the same part again.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about mind wandering and needing to refocus during tasks that require thinking, which most directly relates to difficulty sustaining attention.

patient.answer: I’m not sure with games or recipes, nothing really comes to mind there. The clearest thing for me is still when I sit down with a gallery packet or some notes. I’ll start reading and think I’m following it, but after a few minutes I’m just moving my eyes over the words and my mind has drifted off. Then I have to go back and read that same part again.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences difficulty with attention or mind-wandering during a variety of task types (e.g., conversations, leisure activities, reading) beyond work-related reading tasks, to assess for broader inattention symptoms.
doctor.question: Can you remember if there are times when you're having a conversation, watching something, or doing a leisure activity where you realize your mind has wandered and you have to bring your attention back?

patient.answer: I still don’t really have a good example with a conversation or watching something. The thing I can point to is when I’m reading a gallery packet or notes. I’ll start out okay, but after a few minutes I realize my eyes are still going over the words and I’m not really taking it in, so I have to go back and read that part again.

opening_question.intent: Greet the patient and gather the initial presenting concern
opening_question.question: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports persistent difficulty maintaining attention, primarily during reading and work-related tasks, with consistent awareness of mind-wandering and compensatory re-reading. There is no clear evidence of mood episodes, substance use, or intellectual disability. The symptoms are suggestive of an attention disorder within the F40-F48 category, possibly ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation, though not fully confirmed due to limited functional impairment data.
